text: held worker/T-0140: footprint needs asf/views/readme.py (report: needs writes) — widen_footprint decides

F-0183's own plan (`docs/plans/f-0183.md`, committed here at `f044e81da`) is a careful, well-evidenced piece of work, but the card it plans is a strict subset of F-0179, which the trunk already carries further along. F-0179's approved spec (`7cca3bf8f`, `docs/specs/f-0179.md`, merged to `main` at PR #468 — *before* F-0183's own spec `fac479304` at PR #472) names the identical defect verbatim ("`${{ vars.X || 'heavy' }}` is read today as `heavy` **always**, without ever asking the repo what `X` is... `--apply` strips it") and its scope is a superset: a general expression evaluator (`fromJSON(format(...))`, an event ternary) *plus* exactly F-0183's two halves — reading the repo's own Actions variables (F-0179 Task 3, `S-36352`) and freezing every removal while a `runs-on` is unresolved (F-0179 Task 1, `S-36353`, "the unresolved row, said out loud — and no label removed while one stands"). F-0179's plan (`f372bcaf7`, PR #497) is already on `main`, three Tasks, ready to mint and code; I checked its `Backend.variables()`, `unresolved_rows`, `drift`'s freeze, and `plan`'s three-way split against the checkout and they land on the same `asf/ci_pool.py` functions F-0183's plan targets, with the narrower card's incident (`CI_REQUIRED_LABEL`/`vars.X` on a scalar expression) as one of F-0179's own precondition rows (P3). Coding F-0183 as planned would duplicate F-0179's Task 1 and Task 3 line for line and then conflict with them in the same file. What now holds: F-0183 does no further planning or coding of its own; its incident is closed by F-0179 landing. Nothing in F-0183's plan is wrong — it is superseded outright, not corrected.
